chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) performed the obligatory prayer while in the palanquin (mahmal) on a day of heat and rain.'

key_terms.الْمَحْمِلِ: Palanquin or litter carried by beasts of burden, used for sitting during travel
key_terms.يَوْمٍ وَحٍ: A day of heat or warmth

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray sitting in a palanquin during travel due to heat or rain?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) practical application of *rukhsah* (concession) by praying in a *mahmal* (palanquin) during inclement weather, establishing a precedent for seated prayer when standing causes hardship. In Shia jurisprudence, this supports the broader principle that the severity of the condition determines the extent of the concession, linking physical comfort to the validity of prayer postures. It underscores the flexibility of Islamic law in accommodating human frailty while maintaining ritual integrity.
